info.title: IT Collect - BY 2026
info.description:
IT Collect BY 2026 will utilize the OAuth2 Authorization framework to authenticate vendor client
applications to start using our APIs. A walkthrough of client configuration for Postman is
outlined below. All current documentation and application features are currently undergoing
development.

As part of your vendor application you will need to authenticate via an OAuth 2.0 compatible
client library using the Authorization Code Grant Type. Once a token is received from the
IT Collect OAuth server it will need to be included as part of an HTTP Request Header for
subsequent requests to API endpoints. CURL Example:

```console
curl -X GET "http://itcollect-url-tbd/v1/services"  -H  "Authorization: Bearer YOUR-TOKEN-HERE" -H  "accept: application/ld+json"
```

#### Prerequisites
- Request an OAuth 2 identifer and secret from IT Collect team.
- Request a sandbox user account.
- Provider IT Collect with an OAuth 2.0 compatible callback URL

#### Postman

[Postman](https://www.postman.com/) is an API Client that you can use for communication
with IT Collect.

#### Vendor Steps

1. Create a new Postman Collection and import the OpenAPI spec

2. Edit the Collection

3. Switch to the Authorization tab and select `OAuth 2.0`

4. Click the "Get New Access Token" button leaving Header Prefix as `Bearer`.

| Setting | Value |
| ------------- | ------------- |
| Token Name | Bearer |
| Grant Type | Authorization Code |
| * Callback URL | https://app.getpostman.com/oauth2/callback |
| * Authorize using browser | Yes, enable this option |
| Auth URL | https://itcollect.itdashboard.gov/oauth/authorize |
| Access Token URL | https://itcollect.itdashboard.gov/oauth/token |
| Client ID | *{Request from IT Collect}* |
| Client Secret | *{Request from IT Collect}* |
| * State |  |
| Client Authentication | Send client credentials in body |

> * Callback URL: Vendor application callback URL.  Will depend on individual vendor
implementation.  Must be provided to IT Collect team prior to implementation.
> * Authorize using browser: This option is specific to PostMan and is required for PIV
cards to be used by Login.gov. PostMan cannot read PIVs so a browser is required for this
step.
> * State: This is an optional parameter, leave blank in Postman, but you may provide a
state in your vendor application. You may use this as CSRF protection mechanism or to
assist in maintaining a state such as a session key.

5. Click "Request Token"

6. Login using either your sandbox user account or your login.gov account (see below).

You should now have an access token suitable for defining the HTTP Authorization Header.

#### Login.gov PIV card

PIV (Personal Identity Verification) cards testing steps

1. Once the browser window has opened (you may need to allow popups in your browse for this
domain) click "Login with Login.gov"

2. Provide your Login.gov credentials using either your PIV access card or username and
password credentials.

You should now have an access token suitable for defining in the HTTP Authorization Header.

# Authentication

sharedServiceCode.description:
Shared Services Code, 2 digit - 00, 24, or 48 Select one of the following enumerated codes: - 00: Not Applicable, - 24: E-Gov initiatives or an individual Agency's participation in one of the E-Gov/LoB initiatives, - 48: Any Multi-Agency (Inter- or Intra-Agency) IT collaboration or an individual Agency’s in one of these initiatives, such as use of a centralized FOIA portal.

  • The value you selected is not a valid choice.

sharedServiceId.description:
Shared Services Identifier - 4 digits
These four digits are applicable for all Investments with a Shared Services Category of 24 or 48. A code will be
specifically assigned for all E-Gov/LoB shared services in OMB Circular A-11 Section 55, while Agencies should assign their own
four digit unique codes for Multi-Agency initiatives using the “48” shared services category.

This code represents the same 4-digit identifier previously provided in the last nine digits of the UII for
Investments starting with xxx-99999XXXX.

missionSupportCategories.description:
Mission Support Category - 2 digit code - 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, or 09 These two digits indicate the category of common Mission Support Services Investments by Federal Integrated Business Framework (FIBF) Service Area(s). All non-Mission Support Services Investments should use Category 01. Mission Support Services Investments may select more than one code where applicable: - 01: Not Applicable - 02: Financial Management - 03: Human Resources - 04: Procurement - 05: Travel / Transportation - 06: Grants Management - 07: Electronic Records Management - 08: Cybersecurity Services - 09: Other

bureauCode.description:
Bureau Code (string) - 2 digit code The two digits indicate the bureau code of the Investment (see Appendix C of OMB Circular No. A-11). If this is a department-level or an Agency-wide activity, use “00” as your bureau code.
Validations
  • One of the following Length errors:
    1) This value is too short. It should have 2 characters or more..
    2) This value is too long. It should have 2 characters or less..
    3) Required and must be 2 digits long.
    4) This value does not match the expected UTF-8 charset..
  • This value should be of type digit.
  • This value should be of type digit.

partOfAITPS.description:
Part of AITPS (string) - 2 digit code - 01, 02, or 03 These two digits indicate one of the three parts of the Agency IT Portfolio Summary, to which the Investment belongs: - 01: Part 1. IT Investments for Mission Delivery - 02: Part 2. IT Investments for Mission Support Services - 03: Part 3. IT Investments for IT Infrastructure, IT Security, and IT Management
Validations
  • This value should not be blank.
  • The value you selected is not a valid choice.
  • This value should be of type digit.

standardIdCategory.description:
Standard IT Infrastructure and Management Category 2 digit code - 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07 ,08, 09, or 10 These two digits indicate the sub-category of Investments identified as Part 3: IT Investments for IT Infrastructure, IT Security, and IT Management. All Part 3 Investments should select one of the following codes other than “01: Not Applicable,” while all Part 1 and 2 Investments should select “01: Not Applicable.” - 01: Not Applicable - 02: IT Security and Compliance - 03: IT Management - 04: Network - 05: Data Center and Cloud - 06: End User - 07: Output - 08: Application - 09: Delivery - 10: Platform

  • This value should not be blank.

missionSupportArea.description:

investmentType.description:
Type of Investment - 2 digit code - 01, 02, 03, 04, or 05 These two digits indicate the type of Investment being reported as follows: - 01: Major IT Investments - 02: Non-major IT Investments - 03: IT Migration Investment: The portion of a larger asset and for which there is an existing Business Case for the overall asset. The description of the IT Investment should indicate the UII of the major asset Investment of the managing partner. - 04: Funding Transfer Investments: These are primarily used to indicate the partner contribution to a Lead Agency Investment through inter- or intraAgency transfers. The description of the IT Investment should indicate the UII of the Lead Agency’s Investment. - 05: Standard IT Infrastructure Investments in Part 3: IT Infrastructure, IT Security, IT Management Investments (IT Security and Compliance, IT Management, Network, Data Center and Cloud, End User, Output, Application, Delivery, and Platform).
Validations
  • This value should not be blank.
  • The value you selected is not a valid choice.
  • This value should be of type digit.

nssId.description:

type.description:
Select either O&M or DME.
O&M: Operations & Maintenance Costs refers to the expenses required to operate and maintain an IT asset that is operating in a production environment.
DME: Development, Modernization, and Enhancement refers to projects and activities leading to new IT assets/systems, as well as projects and activities that change or modify existing IT assets to substantively improve capability or performance, implement legislative or regulatory requirements, or meet an Agency leadership request. DME activity may occur at any time during a program’s life cycle.

costPool.description:
For ledger items selecting TBM reporting, Agencies can align funding against a Cost Pool per the
definitions for TBM v3.0 provided online by the TBM Council

ITTower.description:
For ledger items selecting TBM reporting, Agencies can align funding against a IT Tower per the
definitions for TBM v3.0 provided online by the TBM Council

fundingSource.description:
For ledger items selecting Funding Sources Reporting, indicate the Funding Source associated
with a given ledger item.

source.description:
For ledger items selecting Funding Sources Reporting, indicate whether the funding is associated
with 'Agency Funding' or 'Contributions'

ledgerElementStyle.description:
Indicate the type of funding data a given ledger request will provide to IT Collect. This field's
selection will trigger a series of validation checks to ensure that Agencies are providing and omitting the
relevant data points for either Funding Sources or TBM reporting. Funding Sources reporting will mandate the
inclusion of the Funding Source, Source, and Type fields. TBM reporting will mandate the inclusion of either
the Cost Pool or IT Tower field. Budget Authority requests must include the same set of fields as Funding
Source request, however, Budget Authority submissions do not count toward the aggregate funding total of an
investment.

costItem.description:
Optional descriptive name detailing the type of funding information provided within  given
ledger item

year.description: A Fiscal year associated with the funding in a given ledger item

amount.description: Funding amount for a ledger item

type.description:
Select either O&M or DME.
O&M: Operations & Maintenance Costs refers to the expenses required to operate and maintain an IT asset that is operating in a production environment.
DME: Development, Modernization, and Enhancement refers to projects and activities leading to new IT assets/systems, as well as projects and activities that change or modify existing IT assets to substantively improve capability or performance, implement legislative or regulatory requirements, or meet an Agency leadership request. DME activity may occur at any time during a program’s life cycle.

costPool.description:
For ledger items selecting TBM reporting, Agencies can align funding against a Cost Pool per the
definitions for TBM v3.0 provided online by the TBM Council

ITTower.description:
For ledger items selecting TBM reporting, Agencies can align funding against a IT Tower per the
definitions for TBM v3.0 provided online by the TBM Council

fundingSource.description:
For ledger items selecting Funding Sources Reporting, indicate the Funding Source associated
with a given ledger item.

source.description:
For ledger items selecting Funding Sources Reporting, indicate whether the funding is associated
with 'Agency Funding' or 'Contributions'

ledgerElementStyle.description:
Indicate the type of funding data a given ledger request will provide to IT Collect. This field's
selection will trigger a series of validation checks to ensure that Agencies are providing and omitting the
relevant data points for either Funding Sources or TBM reporting. Funding Sources reporting will mandate the
inclusion of the Funding Source, Source, and Type fields. TBM reporting will mandate the inclusion of either
the Cost Pool or IT Tower field. Budget Authority requests must include the same set of fields as Funding
Source request, however, Budget Authority submissions do not count toward the aggregate funding total of an
investment.

alternateBureau.description:
Alternate Bureau (string) - 2 digit code
Enter the Bureau who controls spending for this ledger entry

rebaseLines.description: A list of associated rebaseLine IDs

isMasked.description: A readonly boolean indicating whether the document is masked from the public.

isRetired.description: Boolean indicating if the document has been retired

type.description:
Select either O&M or DME.
O&M: Operations & Maintenance Costs refers to the expenses required to operate and maintain an IT asset that is operating in a production environment.
DME: Development, Modernization, and Enhancement refers to projects and activities leading to new IT assets/systems, as well as projects and activities that change or modify existing IT assets to substantively improve capability or performance, implement legislative or regulatory requirements, or meet an Agency leadership request. DME activity may occur at any time during a program’s life cycle.

definitions for TBM v3.0 provided online by the TBM Council

ITTower.description:
For ledger items selecting TBM reporting, Agencies can align funding against a IT Tower per the

fundingSource.description:
For ledger items selecting Funding Sources Reporting, indicate the Funding Source associated
with a given ledger item.

source.description:
For ledger items selecting Funding Sources Reporting, indicate whether the funding is associated
with 'Agency Funding' or 'Contributions'

ledgerElementStyle.description:
Indicate the type of funding data a given ledger request will provide to IT Collect. This field's
selection will trigger a series of validation checks to ensure that Agencies are providing and omitting the
relevant data points for either Funding Sources or TBM reporting. Funding Sources reporting will mandate the
inclusion of the Funding Source, Source, and Type fields. TBM reporting will mandate the inclusion of either
the Cost Pool or IT Tower field. Budget Authority requests must include the same set of fields as Funding
Source request, however, Budget Authority submissions do not count toward the aggregate funding total of an
investment.

activeRisk.description: For each Risk Area, indicate whether the Investment has identified at least one active risk.

riskProbability.description:
Enter the likelihood that risk associated with each Risk Area will become realized as an issue.
Investments/Services should only report Risk Probability for Risk Areas that reported “Yes” to Active Risk.
For the purposes of standard reporting across Agencies, the following probability benchmarks have been provided
for each response to indicate the estimated likelihood that a given risk will become realized as an issue:
1) Very Low – 0-10%, 2) Low – 11-30%, 3) Medium – 31-60%, 4) High – 61-90%, 5) Very High – 91-100%

riskImpact.description:
Enter the level of a potential negative impact for the Risk Area if realized as an issue.
Investments/Services should only report Risk Impact for Risk Areas that reported “Yes” in Active Risk.

mitigationStrategy.example: description of each individual risk with a combined probability and impact score of 6.
mitigationStrategy.description:
For each Risk Area with a combined probability and impact score of a “10” or greater, provide a short description
of each individual risk with a combined probability and impact score of “10” or greater along with both the
Investment’s mitigation strategy for preventing each risk from becoming realized as an issue and the contingency
plan should the mitigation strategy fail. The mitigation strategy and contingency plan should deal with methods
for avoiding or pre-empting risk as well as addressing any realized issues.
This field is optional for Risk Areas with scores of “9” or lower. Investment/Services should only report
Mitigation Strategy/Contingency Plan data for Risk Areas that reported “Yes” to Active Risk.

riskArea.description:
Provide data for relevant risks related to the A-11 Risk Area below. Definitions
of each Risk Area are provided in Appendix C. Risk Areas include:
Enum:
 1) Technology 2) Project Schedule and Resources 3) Business 4) Organizational and Change Management
 5) Strategic 6) Security 7) Privacy 8) Data 9) Integration 10) Project Team 11) Requirements 12) Cost
 13) Project Management 14) Climate

riskScore.description: A system generated field that is auto-calculated on every submission based on (riskImpact x riskProbability).

currentUII.description:
The Current UII includes an Agency code and a nine-digit unique identifier.
Variable information formerly included in the UII of previous years is not part
of the UII primary key.

title.description:
This is a text field to provide the Investment title. To the extent that they are not
part of the name used by the Agency, other identifiers such as bureaus or other
numeric codes should not be included as part of an Investment title.

description.example: Sample description of the IT Dashboard modernization process.
description.description:
Description for each Investment. This description should briefly explain the
purpose of the Investment and what program(s) it supports, including the value
to the public.

changeInStatus.description:
This is used when an Investment has a change in status (e.g., downgraded to non-major IT Investment,
eliminated, retired, consolidated, split) for the current budget submission relative to the previous budget
cycle. The change of status should be indicated with one of the following reasons:

- 01: Upgraded from non-major to major IT Investment
- 02: Downgraded from major to non-major IT Investment
- 03: Split into multiple Investments
- 04: Consolidation of Investments
- 05: Reorganization
- 06: Eliminated by funding
- 07: Eliminated by split
- 08: Eliminated by consolidation
- 09: Eliminated by reorganization
- 10: New
- 11: No Change in Status

changeInStatusDescription.description:
This is used when an indicator has been chosen for "Change in Investment Status Identifier" in
order to provide a description of the rationale for the change, which may include impacted UIIs, specific
references to legislative requirements, or governance board decisions and effective dates.

previousUIIs.description:
Previous UIIs
are identifiers depicting the Agency Code and unique investment number
used to report the Investment in the previous BY Agency IT Portfolio
Summary submission to OMB. Each UII in the array must correspond with active
or formerly active UIIs in IT Collect. All Investments where Change in
Status does not equal “new” must provide Previous UII data.

sharedServiceCode.description:
Shared Services Code, 2 digit - 00, 24, or 48

Select one of the following enumerated codes:
- 00: Not Applicable,
- 24: E-Gov initiatives or an individual Agency's participation in one of the E-Gov/LoB initiatives,
- 48: Any Multi-Agency (Inter- or Intra-Agency) IT collaboration or an individual Agency’s in one of these
initiatives, such as use of a centralized FOIA portal.

sharedServiceId.description:
Shared Services Identifier - 4 digits
These four digits are applicable for all Investments with a Shared Services Category of 24 or 48. A code will be
specifically assigned for all E-Gov/LoB shared services in OMB Circular A-11 Section 55, while Agencies should assign their own
four digit unique codes for Multi-Agency initiatives using the “48” shared services category.

This code represents the same 4-digit identifier previously provided in the last nine digits of the UII for
Investments starting with xxx-99999XXXX.

missionSupportCategories.description:
Mission Support Category - 2 digit code - 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, or 09
These two digits indicate the category of common Mission Support Services
Investments by Federal Integrated Business Framework (FIBF) Service Area(s).
All non-Mission Support Services Investments should use Category 01. Mission
Support Services Investments may select more than one code where applicable:

- 01: Not Applicable
- 02: Financial Management
- 03: Human Resources
- 04: Procurement
- 05: Travel / Transportation
- 06: Grants Management
- 07: Electronic Records Management
- 08: Cybersecurity Services
- 09: Other

bureauCode.description:
Bureau Code (string) - 2 digit code
The two digits indicate the bureau code of the Investment (see Appendix C of OMB Circular No. A-11).
If this is a department-level or an Agency-wide  activity, use “00” as your bureau code.

partOfAITPS.description:
Part of AITPS (string) - 2 digit code - 01, 02, or 03
These two digits indicate one of the three parts of the Agency IT Portfolio
Summary, to which the Investment belongs:

- 01: Part 1. IT Investments for Mission Delivery
- 02: Part 2. IT Investments for Mission Support Services
- 03: Part 3. IT Investments for IT Infrastructure, IT Security, and IT Management

standardIdCategory.description:
Standard IT Infrastructure and Management Category
2 digit code - 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07 ,08, 09, or 10
These two digits indicate the sub-category of Investments identified as Part 3:
IT Investments for IT Infrastructure, IT Security, and IT Management.

All Part 3 Investments should select one of the following codes other than “01: Not
Applicable,” while all Part 1 and 2 Investments should select “01: Not Applicable.”

- 01: Not Applicable
- 02: IT Security and Compliance
- 03: IT Management
- 04: Network
- 05: Data Center and Cloud
- 06: End User
- 07: Output
- 08: Application
- 09: Delivery
- 10: Platform

missionSupportArea.description:
Mission Delivery and Management Support Area  - 2 digit code
These two digits indicate the mission delivery and management support areas.
Agencies should assign a unique code for each mission delivery and
management support area reported.

investmentType.description:
Type of Investment - 2 digit code - 01, 02, 03, 04, or 05
These two digits indicate the type of Investment being reported as follows:

- 01: Major IT Investments
- 02: Non-major IT Investments
- 03: IT Migration Investment: The portion of a larger asset and for which there is an existing Business Case
for the overall asset. The description of the IT Investment should indicate the UII of the major asset Investment
of the managing partner.
- 04: Funding Transfer Investments: These are primarily used to indicate the partner contribution to a Lead
Agency Investment through inter- or intraAgency transfers. The description of the IT Investment should indicate
the UII of the Lead Agency’s Investment.
- 05: Standard IT Infrastructure Investments in Part 3: IT Infrastructure, IT  Security, IT Management
Investments (IT Security and Compliance, IT Management, Network, Data Center and Cloud, End User, Output,
Application, Delivery, and Platform).

nssId.description:
National Security Systems Identifier - 2 digit code - 01 or 02
These two digits indicate whether the Investment is a National Security System the Federal Information Security
Management Act of 2002 (FISMA), 44 U.S.C. 3542(b)(2) as follows:

- 01: Non-National Security System Investment
- 02: National Security System Investment (these investments will not be publicly viewable on the IT Dashboard)

publicUrls.description:
Public URL(s) List any website or digital service that is supported primarily by this Investment.
Supply an array of strings (URLs).

description.example: Sample description of the IT Dashboard modernization process.
description.description:
Description for each Investment. This description should briefly explain the
purpose of the Investment and what program(s) it supports, including the value
to the public.

changeInStatus.description:
This is used when an Investment has a change in status (e.g., downgraded to non-major IT Investment,
eliminated, retired, consolidated, split) for the current budget submission relative to the previous budget
cycle. The change of status should be indicated with one of the following reasons:

- 01: Upgraded from non-major to major IT Investment
- 02: Downgraded from major to non-major IT Investment
- 03: Split into multiple Investments
- 04: Consolidation of Investments
- 05: Reorganization
- 06: Eliminated by funding
- 07: Eliminated by split
- 08: Eliminated by consolidation
- 09: Eliminated by reorganization
- 10: New
- 11: No Change in Status

changeInStatusDescription.description:
This is used when an indicator has been chosen for "Change in Investment Status Identifier" in
order to provide a description of the rationale for the change, which may include impacted UIIs, specific
references to legislative requirements, or governance board decisions and effective dates.

previousUIIs.description:
Previous UIIs
are identifiers depicting the Agency Code and unique investment number
used to report the Investment in the previous BY Agency IT Portfolio
Summary submission to OMB. Each UII in the array must correspond with active
or formerly active UIIs in IT Collect. All Investments where Change in
Status does not equal “new” must provide Previous UII data.

sharedServiceCode.description:
Shared Services Code, 2 digit - 00, 24, or 48

Select one of the following enumerated codes:
- 00: Not Applicable,
- 24: E-Gov initiatives or an individual Agency's participation in one of the E-Gov/LoB initiatives,
- 48: Any Multi-Agency (Inter- or Intra-Agency) IT collaboration or an individual Agency’s in one of these
initiatives, such as use of a centralized FOIA portal.

sharedServiceId.description:
Shared Services Identifier - 4 digits
These four digits are applicable for all Investments with a Shared Services Category of 24 or 48. A code will be
specifically assigned for all E-Gov/LoB shared services in OMB Circular A-11 Section 55, while Agencies should assign their own
four digit unique codes for Multi-Agency initiatives using the “48” shared services category.

This code represents the same 4-digit identifier previously provided in the last nine digits of the UII for
Investments starting with xxx-99999XXXX.

missionSupportCategories.description:
Mission Support Category - 2 digit code - 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, or 09
These two digits indicate the category of common Mission Support Services
Investments by Federal Integrated Business Framework (FIBF) Service Area(s).
All non-Mission Support Services Investments should use Category 01. Mission
Support Services Investments may select more than one code where applicable:

- 01: Not Applicable
- 02: Financial Management
- 03: Human Resources
- 04: Procurement
- 05: Travel / Transportation
- 06: Grants Management
- 07: Electronic Records Management
- 08: Cybersecurity Services
- 09: Other

bureauCode.description:
Bureau Code (string) - 2 digit code
The two digits indicate the bureau code of the Investment (see Appendix C of OMB Circular No. A-11).
If this is a department-level or an Agency-wide  activity, use “00” as your bureau code.

partOfAITPS.description:
Part of AITPS (string) - 2 digit code - 01, 02, or 03
These two digits indicate one of the three parts of the Agency IT Portfolio
Summary, to which the Investment belongs:

- 01: Part 1. IT Investments for Mission Delivery
- 02: Part 2. IT Investments for Mission Support Services
- 03: Part 3. IT Investments for IT Infrastructure, IT Security, and IT Management

standardIdCategory.description:
Standard IT Infrastructure and Management Category
2 digit code - 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07 ,08, 09, or 10
These two digits indicate the sub-category of Investments identified as Part 3:
IT Investments for IT Infrastructure, IT Security, and IT Management.

All Part 3 Investments should select one of the following codes other than “01: Not
Applicable,” while all Part 1 and 2 Investments should select “01: Not Applicable.”

- 01: Not Applicable
- 02: IT Security and Compliance
- 03: IT Management
- 04: Network
- 05: Data Center and Cloud
- 06: End User
- 07: Output
- 08: Application
- 09: Delivery
- 10: Platform

missionSupportArea.description:
Mission Delivery and Management Support Area  - 2 digit code
These two digits indicate the mission delivery and management support areas.
Agencies should assign a unique code for each mission delivery and
management support area reported.

investmentType.description:
Type of Investment - 2 digit code - 01, 02, 03, 04, or 05
These two digits indicate the type of Investment being reported as follows:

- 01: Major IT Investments
- 02: Non-major IT Investments
- 03: IT Migration Investment: The portion of a larger asset and for which there is an existing Business Case
for the overall asset. The description of the IT Investment should indicate the UII of the major asset Investment
of the managing partner.
- 04: Funding Transfer Investments: These are primarily used to indicate the partner contribution to a Lead
Agency Investment through inter- or intraAgency transfers. The description of the IT Investment should indicate
the UII of the Lead Agency’s Investment.
- 05: Standard IT Infrastructure Investments in Part 3: IT Infrastructure, IT  Security, IT Management
Investments (IT Security and Compliance, IT Management, Network, Data Center and Cloud, End User, Output,
Application, Delivery, and Platform).

nssId.description:
National Security Systems Identifier - 2 digit code - 01 or 02
These two digits indicate whether the Investment is a National Security System the Federal Information Security
Management Act of 2002 (FISMA), 44 U.S.C. 3542(b)(2) as follows:

- 01: Non-National Security System Investment
- 02: National Security System Investment (these investments will not be publicly viewable on the IT Dashboard)

All non-Mission Support Services Investments should use Category 01. Mission
Support Services Investments may select more than one code where applicable:

- 01: Not Applicable
- 02: Financial Management
- 03: Human Resources
- 04: Procurement
- 05: Travel / Transportation
- 06: Grants Management
- 07: Electronic Records Management
- 08: Cybersecurity Services
- 09: Other

bureauCode.description:
Bureau Code (string) - 2 digit code
The two digits indicate the bureau code of the Investment (see Appendix C of OMB Circular No. A-11).
If this is a department-level or an Agency-wide  activity, use “00” as your bureau code.

partOfAITPS.description:
Part of AITPS (string) - 2 digit code - 01, 02, or 03
These two digits indicate one of the three parts of the Agency IT Portfolio
Summary, to which the Investment belongs:

- 01: Part 1. IT Investments for Mission Delivery
- 02: Part 2. IT Investments for Mission Support Services
- 03: Part 3. IT Investments for IT Infrastructure, IT Security, and IT Management

standardIdCategory.description:
Standard IT Infrastructure and Management Category
2 digit code - 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07 ,08, 09, or 10
These two digits indicate the sub-category of Investments identified as Part 3:
IT Investments for IT Infrastructure, IT Security, and IT Management.

All Part 3 Investments should select one of the following codes other than “01: Not
Applicable,” while all Part 1 and 2 Investments should select “01: Not Applicable.”

- 01: Not Applicable
- 02: IT Security and Compliance
- 03: IT Management
- 04: Network
- 05: Data Center and Cloud
- 06: End User
- 07: Output
- 08: Application
- 09: Delivery
- 10: Platform

missionSupportArea.description:
Mission Delivery and Management Support Area  - 2 digit code
These two digits indicate the mission delivery and management support areas.
Agencies should assign a unique code for each mission delivery and
management support area reported.

investmentType.description:
Type of Investment - 2 digit code - 01, 02, 03, 04, or 05
These two digits indicate the type of Investment being reported as follows:

- 01: Major IT Investments
- 02: Non-major IT Investments
- 03: IT Migration Investment: The portion of a larger asset and for which there is an existing Business Case
for the overall asset. The description of the IT Investment should indicate the UII of the major asset Investment
of the managing partner.
- 04: Funding Transfer Investments: These are primarily used to indicate the partner contribution to a Lead
Agency Investment through inter- or intraAgency transfers. The description of the IT Investment should indicate
the UII of the Lead Agency’s Investment.
- 05: Standard IT Infrastructure Investments in Part 3: IT Infrastructure, IT  Security, IT Management
Investments (IT Security and Compliance, IT Management, Network, Data Center and Cloud, End User, Output,
Application, Delivery, and Platform).

nssId.description:
National Security Systems Identifier - 2 digit code - 01 or 02
These two digits indicate whether the Investment is a National Security System the Federal Information Security
Management Act of 2002 (FISMA), 44 U.S.C. 3542(b)(2) as follows:

- 01: Non-National Security System Investment
- 02: National Security System Investment (these investments will not be publicly viewable on the IT Dashboard)

publicUrls.description:
Public URL(s) List any website or digital service that is supported primarily by this Investment.
Supply an array of strings (URLs).

type.description:
Select either O&M or DME.
O&M: Operations & Maintenance Costs refers to the expenses required to operate and maintain an IT asset that is operating in a production environment.
DME: Development, Modernization, and Enhancement refers to projects and activities leading to new IT assets/systems, as well as projects and activities that change or modify existing IT assets to substantively improve capability or performance, implement legislative or regulatory requirements, or meet an Agency leadership request. ledgerElementStyle.description:
Indicate the type of funding data a given ledger request will provide to IT Collect. This field's
selection will trigger a series of validation checks to ensure that Agencies are providing and omitting the
relevant data points for either Funding Sources or TBM reporting. Funding Sources reporting will mandate the
inclusion of the Funding Source, Source, and Type fields. TBM reporting will mandate the inclusion of either
the Cost Pool or IT Tower field. Budget Authority requests must include the same set of fields as Funding
Source request, however, Budget Authority submissions do not count toward the aggregate funding total of an
investment.
